chunks: Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Hammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying regarding this verse:
'Nay, it is clear signs in the chests of those who have been given knowledge'
and he gestured with his hand toward his own chest.

key_terms.آيَاتٌ بَيِّنَاتٌ: Clear signs/verses — the Quran's miraculous nature and divine guidance
key_terms.أَوْمَأَ: Gestured/pointed — a physical act confirming the interpretation through bodily indication
key_terms.صُدُورِ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ: Chests of those given knowledge — interpreted as the Imams of the Ahlulbayt

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the verse 'clear signs in the chests of those given knowledge'?
ai.summary: Abu Baseer narrates that he heard Imam al-Baqir (AS) interpret Quran 29:49 — 'clear signs in the chests of those who have been given knowledge' — by pointing to his own chest, indicating that the Imams of the Ahlulbayt are the ones in whose chests these divine signs reside. This is a cornerstone narration for the Shia doctrine of the Imams as the repositories of divine knowledge, explaining that the 'those given knowledge' in the verse are the Imams themselves. The gestural commentary (pointing to his chest) transforms a textual interpretation into a living embodied claim.
